findings.text: Each season from 2017-2026, Locksmith only used bet rules that had already worked in earlier seasons, then graded them at the real line and price each rule would have bet (the closing line, or the SportsBookReview opener for opening-line rules). Record: 532-448-23, 54.3% wins, +41.8 units (+4.2% return). Most of it comes from wind unders; the rest from line-move bets at the opener (2018-2021, the seasons with real openers) and big disagreements with the spread. Every other bet type (early totals, ‘price value’, public-money fades) failed this test and was removed.

findings.title: Locksmith is as accurate as Las Vegas at predicting games
findings.text: Over 3,402 games it missed the final margin by 9.92 points on average; the closing betting line missed by 9.91. That is a statistical tie with the sharpest number in sports.

findings.title: The real edge: totals, early in the week
findings.text: When Locksmith’s early-week model disagrees with the opening total by 2+ points, the line moves toward Locksmith about 65% of the time. Bet those totals early. Once the line has moved, the edge is gone.

findings.title: Home favorites are slightly overpriced
findings.text: Since 2006 home favorites covered only 48.0% of the time (3,403 games). Sportsbooks shade these lines because the public loves favorites. Small edge, best as a tiebreaker.

findings.title: Sportsbooks under-react to wind
findings.text: Each mph of wind above 10 lowers scoring by about 0.38 points, but the line only moves 0.09. Strong-wind unders are a real edge.

findings.title: QB injury news is priced correctly
findings.text: When a starting quarterback changes, sportsbooks move the line about the right amount. No edge there.

findings.title: Public-betting tricks don’t reliably work
findings.text: On 902 real games with actual betting percentages, betting against the side a book is ‘holding’ won 51%, following reverse line moves won 49%. You need 52.4% to profit. These are shown for context only.

findings.title: Two betting-percentage signals worth watching
findings.text: When big bettors pile onto a total (money far above ticket count), that side won 55% of 237 games, and fading 70%+ of the public on spreads won 55%. Promising but not proven yet.

findings.title: Player projections beat ‘last six games’ where it matters
findings.text: Tested on every 2025 game: passing yards miss 59 yards versus 67 for a simple recent average, and touchdown odds are far better calibrated. For catches, targets and rushing, recent usage is about as good as anything.

findings.title: The score simulator is honest about uncertainty
findings.text: Real final scores landed inside Locksmith’s ‘80% likely’ range 82% of the time, and it reproduces how often games end on 3 and 7.

findings.title: Most edges disappear by kickoff
findings.text: Locksmith’s numbers beat the opening line but not the closing line, and the ‘early total’ bets lost money when bought late. Only the rules that survive at the closing price are bet any time; line-move bets (away side / under when the model expects the line to move that way) are worth about +1.4 points of closing-line value but only at the opener, so they are bet only when Locksmith captures a real opener itself.

findings.title: Popular betting angles are already priced in
findings.text: Referees, Thursday games, division games, prime time, altitude and teams playing on their body clock all showed no edge against the closing line.
